round_analysis.summary: Round 0 probed nine single-axis augmentation arms against a no-augmentation baseline (weighted F1 = 0.7130) on 690 sarcasm samples with BERT+SVM and 5-fold CV. No arm produced a PRIMARY-metric gain that exceeds its own seed noise: the best, back-translation with a sarcasm-cue guard (P04, 0.7146, +0.0016 vs baseline), is smaller than the 0.003-0.008 noise_std observed in comparable arms, and context-only synonym replacement (P05, +0.0003) is well inside its own noise_std of 0.0021. Three arms degraded beyond their noise band: speaker anonymization (P08, -0.0100), context-window truncation (P07, -0.0065, noise 0.0032) and joint utterance+context synonym replacement (P06, -0.0041, noise 0.0007). All arms paid a large relative processing-time cost, with context-only synonym replacement at ~997 s and strong 4x synonym at ~139 s. The round's information value is mainly in ruling out uniform full-corpus replication and in identifying which components must not be perturbed.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity was essentially faithful (realized multipliers matched designed final_multiplier for all arms except P02, which realized 3.80x instead of 4x because dedupe_identical_copies removed near-duplicate synonym copies). The core claim that label-preserving paraphrase/lexical noise improves fold-averaged weighted F1 is NOT supported: the largest gain (P04, +0.0016) is below the seed variability seen elsewhere in the round, and every lexical arm (P01, P02, P03) sits at or below baseline. Sub-question (b) on the perturbation ceiling is supported: semantics- or structure-destroying edits (P08 speaker anonymization -0.0100; P07 context truncation -0.0065; P09 deletion -0.0057) fall at or beyond their noise bands, whereas mild meaning-preserving edits are merely neutral. Sub-question (a) on which component to perturb is answered only weakly: utterance-only and context-only are both neutral, but combining them (P06) is measurably worse than either.

key_findings: Uniform replication of every training row appears to be the limiting factor rather than the specific operator: P01/P02/P03/P05 span WordNet, MLM and context-only edits at 2x-3.8x and all land within ~0.002 of baseline, i.e. inside noise. Hypothesized mechanism: for an SVM on frozen BERT sentence embeddings, near-duplicate copies mostly re-weight the same support region without adding decision-boundary information, so the effective sample size barely grows.

Controlled component comparison at matched 10% strength: utterance-only (P01, -0.0023, noise 0.0070) and context-only (P05, +0.0003, noise 0.0021) are neutral, but the joint arm P06 (-0.0041, noise 0.0007) is worse than both with the tightest noise band in the round. Hypothesis: simultaneous perturbation of utterance and context degrades the utterance-context incongruity signal that carries sarcasm, an effect that neither single-component arm exposes.

Speaker anonymization (P08, -0.0100, noise_std 0.0) is the largest degradation and the only arm that rewrites all four text fields. Two competing hypotheses: character identity is a genuine predictive feature for this TV-show corpus (Chandler/Sheldon-style sarcasm priors), or the augmented SPEAKER_A/B surface form creates a train-only text distribution never seen in the untouched validation folds. These are not separable from this round's evidence.

Context-window truncation (P07, -0.0065, noise 0.0032) harms F1 despite editing no wording and costing ~0.025 s, indicating the BERT encoding of longer preceding turns carries usable signal; shortening context is a lossy transformation, not a free 'view'. It is also the cheapest non-trivial arm, so its failure is not a compute-budget issue.
positive_signals: Back-translation with the sarcasm-cue guard (P04, back_translate + sarcasm_cue_guard_filter, utterance only, 2x) is the only arm above baseline (0.7146, +0.0016); direction is favourable but the magnitude is not separable from seed noise seen in sibling arms, so it is a candidate to re-test with repeated seeds rather than a confirmed win.

Context-only mild synonym replacement (P05, replace_ratio 0.12, 3x) is the only other non-negative arm (+0.0003) and shows the smallest degradation risk among context edits, suggesting the context field tolerates lexical noise better than it tolerates structural truncation (P07).

Higher strength/volume did not collapse performance: P02 (replace_ratio 0.20, ~3.8x) matches baseline (-0.00005) while P01 (ratio 0.10, 2x) is slightly lower, so within WordNet substitution the usable strength band extends at least to 20% token replacement without meaning-driven damage.
negative_signals: Semantics-free noise controls behaved as designed but confirm no free regularization: random_token_delete (P09, -0.0057, noise 0.0036) and local_window_shuffle (P10, -0.0058, noise 0.0079) are both at or below baseline, so generic distortion of the utterance gives no benefit to the frozen-embedding SVM.

speaker_name_anonymize (P08) removed ~1 point of weighted F1 for a 2x multiplier at negligible cost, making full-field identity normalization the clearest operator to avoid in its current train-only form.
context_window_truncate (P07) degrades beyond its noise band, indicating that resampling context length is not a label-preserving 'view' for this encoder.
tradeoffs: P04 (best PRIMARY) costs 33.2 s versus 0.005 s baseline and yields only a 2x multiplier - the highest F1 per copy but a ~6800x relative time increase for a gain inside the noise band.

P05 buys its +0.0003 (noise-level) gain at 997 s, by far the worst time-to-benefit ratio in the round; P06 achieves a strictly larger edit scope in 1.98 s, so the cost of P05 is not justified by its scope.
P02 reaches the largest realized multiplier (3.80x) at 138.8 s but no PRIMARY benefit, showing multiplier growth alone does not translate to F1 for this model.

The cheapest arms (P07 0.025 s, P08 0.022 s, P09 0.009 s, P10 0.010 s) are also the most harmful, so low augmentation cost in this task correlates with lossy rather than meaning-preserving transformations.
uncertainties: Processing-time measurements look internally inconsistent and should be treated as unreliable: P05 (context-only synonym, 997 s) is ~500x slower than P06 (same operator on utterance AND context, 1.98 s), and P02 is ~250x slower than P01 for only ~3x the work. This suggests differing implementations, caching, or one-off model/resource loading rather than true operator cost, and it also raises doubt about whether P05 and P06 applied identical substitution logic.

noise_std is 0.0 for P04 and P08, implying a single seed or deterministic pipeline; their deltas therefore have no measured stability estimate and the +0.0016 for P04 cannot be confirmed as exceeding seed variation.

It is unclear whether the harmful arms (P07, P08) fail because they destroy label-relevant signal or because they create a train/validation surface-form mismatch, since validation folds were left original in all arms - this confound is shared across the entire round.
leads_from_this_round: Re-test the paraphrase family (back_translate + sarcasm_cue_guard_filter, utterance only) with multiple seeds and additional pivot languages or 2-3 copies, to determine whether P04's +0.0016 survives noise; expect a further processing-time increase from the current 33 s, so pair it with a cheap arm for the cost comparison.

Move away from uniform full-corpus replication toward selective augmentation - e.g. augmenting only a subset of rows (short utterances, minority-class, or low-margin/hard examples) at the same 2x-3x budget - since every full-replication arm landed within noise of baseline while adding size multiplier.

Disentangle the speaker-identity result: apply speaker_name_anonymize consistently to both training and validation text (or restrict it to context_speakers only) to separate 'identity is signal' from 'train-only surface mismatch'; current train-only application cost -0.0100 weighted F1 at near-zero time.

Probe context edits that preserve length instead of truncating: the contrast between context-only lexical noise (P05, neutral) and context_window_truncate (P07, -0.0065) suggests wording-level context perturbation is tolerated while structural shortening is not; keep preserve_context_length true and vary replace_ratio.

round_analysis.summary: Six arms were measured against a 0.7130 baseline (history best 0.7146). Only P14 (cross-example same-label context grafting) improved on baseline (0.71759, +0.0046) and set a new history best (+0.0030), but the gain is smaller than its own noise_std (0.0068), so it is a direction rather than a confirmed win. P13 (random-row-selected mixed paraphrase) was baseline-neutral (-0.0002, noise_std 0.0104). P17 (in-distribution character-name swap) was mildly below baseline (-0.0045, noise_std 0.0065) but clearly better than round-0's out-of-distribution placeholder arm (-0.0100). P11 (multi-pivot back-translation, -0.0069, single-seed) reversed P04's favourable direction, and the two 'information-injection' arms with strong assumptions failed: P15 (LLM synthesis, -0.0227 at 4x its noise_std, 570 s) and P16 (incongruity amplification, -0.0105 at ~9x its noise_std, but only 1.46x realized multiplier vs 3.0 designed). The margin-selection arm (P12) that P13 was designed to control is absent from the gradient, leaving the selection sub-hypothesis untested.

hypothesis_result.reason: The 'new information via cross-example recombination' branch is the only one with a favourable measured direction (P14, best of round and history), though its +0.0046 vs baseline is within its noise_std (0.0068). The 'external generative content' branch is contradicted (P15 -0.0227, well outside noise), and the 'label-conditioned incongruity sharpening' branch is contradicted at the measured level but with a fidelity deviation (P16 realized 1.46x vs designed 3.0x, so the family was tested at roughly half the intended dose). The 'selective, decision-boundary-targeted augmentation' branch is inconclusive because only the random-selection control (P13) appears in the gradient; without its margin-selected twin, the selection criterion cannot be isolated. P11 also realized 2.15x vs designed 3.0x, so its negative result is partly a yield result.

key_findings: P14 (build_same_label_donor_pool + graft_donor_context, copies_per_row=2, scope=context only) is the round and history best (0.71759; +0.0046 vs baseline, +0.0030 vs history best) at the highest realized multiplier (2.997) and negligible cost (0.14 s). Mechanism hypothesis: recombining an utterance with a different same-label context creates pairings no within-example edit can produce, which may discourage the BERT+SVM pipeline from memorizing specific dialogue-topic surface cues and push it toward label-general utterance/context incongruity features. Caveat: the delta is below noise_std (0.0068), and the arm simultaneously varies multiplier (3x vs e.g. P16's 1.46x), so 'more effective rows' is an unresolved confounder.

P15 (llm_novel_utterance_synthesis + llm_label_conditioned_rewrite, 2.90x, 570 s) is the clearest degradation of the round (-0.0227 vs baseline, ~4x its noise_std 0.0058). Two non-exclusive hypotheses: (a) synthesized 'sitcom register' utterances sit outside the corpus's surface distribution, so BERT features of training rows drift away from untouched validation rows; (b) in step s2 the label is asserted by the generation condition and never verified, injecting label noise into roughly half the generated rows. The near-duplicate filter at 0.9 could not catch either failure mode.

P16 (amplify_incongruity_sarcastic / matched_neutral_edit_nonsarcastic) degraded F1 by -0.0105 with an unusually small noise_std (0.0012), i.e. a consistent rather than seed-driven loss, yet realized only 1.458x of the designed 3.0x. Because only rows containing substitutable evaluative adjectives could be edited, the surviving copies are hypothesized to be a lexically skewed subset (polarity-heavy rows over-weighted), so the arm may be measuring a row-selection skew rather than the incongruity-amplification idea itself.

Speaker-identity family: P17's in-distribution bijective name swap (-0.0045, noise_std 0.0065, exact 3.0x) lands closer to baseline than round-0's placeholder version (-0.0100), consistent with the hypothesis that part of the earlier damage came from train-only out-of-distribution surface tokens rather than from destroying identity signal; but it still does not reach baseline, so a residual cost of perturbing speaker identity across both utterance and context at 3x cannot be excluded.
positive_signals: Context-only cross-example grafting (P14) with same-label donors: best primary metric in history, highest realized multiplier, and lowest processing time among generative arms.

Concentrating 5 copies on a random stratified 30% of rows (P13) is primary-metric neutral (-0.0002, within noise_std 0.0104), so heavy per-row duplication on a subset is not inherently harmful and remains a usable substrate for future selection experiments.
Keeping augmented text in the corpus's own name vocabulary (P17) recovers roughly half the round-0 speaker-anonymization loss, supporting in-distribution surface constraints as a general design rule.
negative_signals: External LLM generation with unverified generated labels (P15) is strongly harmful and by far the most expensive arm (570 s).
Lexicon-based label-conditioned polarity editing (P16) is consistently harmful and had the worst yield (1.46x realized vs 3.0x designed).

Multi-pivot back-translation diversity (P11) did not extend P04's favourable direction (-0.0069 vs baseline) and cost 348 s with only 2.15x realized; its noise_std of 0.0 indicates a single seed, so the magnitude is unverified.
tradeoffs: P14 shows no adverse trade-off: best F1, ~3x multiplier, and effectively zero processing time; this makes it the cheapest candidate to scale or replicate.

The two most expensive arms (P15 570 s, P11 348 s) are also the two worst on F1, so processing time buys nothing in this round; however single-run timing has no repeated-run variance and should be treated as indicative only.
P16 pairs its F1 loss with a much lower multiplier (1.46x), so any comparison against 3x arms conflates operator effect with augmentation dose.
uncertainties: The margin-selected arm (P12) referenced by P13's design is missing from the measured gradient, so the entire 'hard-example selection' sub-hypothesis is untested and P13 stands as an unpaired control.

P14's advantage (+0.0046) is smaller than its noise_std (0.0068) and comes from a single configuration (2 copies, uniform same-label donors, no similarity restriction); whether the effect is real, and whether it comes from label-consistent recombination or simply from more distinct rows, is unresolved.

Realized-vs-designed multiplier shortfalls in P11 (2.15/3.0), P16 (1.46/3.0) and P13 (2.12/2.5) mean those families were evaluated at doses below design; their negative results are yield-confounded, and P11's noise_std of 0.0 suggests only one seed was run.
leads_from_this_round: Scale and stress-test cross-example context grafting (graft_donor_context, scope=context only): vary copies_per_row and donor selection (uniform same-label vs similarity- or speaker-constrained donors), and add a cross-label grafting arm as a negative control to test whether the label really travels with the utterance; run multiple seeds since the current gain sits inside noise_std 0.0068.

Re-instate the margin-based selection arm to pair with P13's random-selection control (identical paraphrase_mixed_generator settings, identical copy count and multiplier) so the selection criterion can finally be isolated; P13 shows the substrate itself is F1-neutral.

If LLM content is revisited, drop the unverified llm_novel_utterance_synthesis step and keep only label-preserving rewrites, adding a label-consistency/round-trip verification filter and a stricter register constraint; current evidence (-0.0227 with 570 s) makes unfiltered synthesis a poor risk/cost bet.

round_analysis.summary: Round 2 tested whether the round-1 recombination direction scales, whether it depends on donor label, and whether four never-tested information sources help. Only the recombination family produced a gain: P21 (same-label context grafting, 3 copies, realized 4.00x) reached weighted F1 0.7266, +0.0135 vs baseline (noise_std 0.0090) and +0.0090 vs the round-1/history best, at negligible cost (0.032s). Its dose-matched cross-label control P22 fell to 0.6937 (-0.0193 vs baseline, noise_std 0.0108), i.e. ~0.024 below the same-label arm at identical 3.0x dose, which is the round's cleanest controlled result. All four new/repaired families were at or below baseline: margin-based hard-example selection (P23, -0.0048, inside its noise_std 0.0065), same-label neighbour concatenation (P25, -0.0015, inside noise 0.0058), speaker attribution rendering (P24, -0.0127), label-verified LLM rewriting (P26, -0.0142) and single-pivot back-translation at 3.0x (P27, -0.0127). Cost spread was extreme: 0.009-0.032s for grafting arms vs 230s (P27) and 289s (P26).

hypothesis_result.reason: The recombination half of the hypothesis was implemented faithfully (P21 realized 3.9993x vs designed 4.0x with 3 copies; P22 realized 3.0x, matched to P14) and was supported: the effect persisted and grew with dose/copies (+0.0135 vs baseline, ~1.5x its own noise_std) and the cross-label control separated by ~0.024, indicating label-consistent recombination rather than generic row diversity. The 'untouched information sources' half was not supported: margin selection, additive speaker attribution, similarity concatenation, verified LLM rewriting and replicated back-translation all landed at or below baseline. Two arms have fidelity caveats that keep their sub-conclusions weaker: P25 realized 3.91x although the design declared a 3.0x/2.0x two-point sweep (only one aggregate number reported), and P27 reported a single value at 3.0x with noise_std 0.0 despite a declared two-dose, three-seed design.

key_findings: P21 (graft_donor_context, scope=context only, copies_per_row=3, realized 4.00x) is the new history best at 0.7266, +0.0135 vs baseline and +0.0090 vs last-round best P14 (same operator, 2 copies, 3.0x). The direction is now above its own noise_std (0.0090) rather than inside it as in round 1, so the recombination mechanism is more credible; however copies and multiplier were raised together, so 'more distinct pairings per utterance' and 'more total rows' remain conflated.

The dose-matched control P22 (build_cross_label_donor_pool + graft_donor_context, 3.0x, 2 copies) is 0.0193 below baseline and ~0.024 below the same-label arm at identical dose, a gap far larger than either noise_std (~0.010). Hypothesis: the previous context carries genuine label-relevant evidence in this corpus, so pairing an utterance with an opposite-label context injects label noise; the benefit of grafting is therefore label-consistent recombination, not row-count diversity.

Model-state difficulty selection was not an informative axis: P23 (select_low_margin_rows, fraction 0.3, identical paraphrase generator to P13) sits at -0.0048 vs baseline with noise_std 0.0065, i.e. indistinguishable from both baseline and P13's random-selection -0.0002. Together with P25's near-null result, this suggests the bottleneck is not which rows get paraphrased but that utterance-level lexical edits carry no new decision-boundary information for frozen BERT+SVM. Confounders: P23 realized only 2.29x vs designed 2.5x, and its 9.06s cost buys nothing.

All three surface-rewriting/rendering arms that make training rows stylistically unlike the untouched validation rows lost 0.013-0.019 F1 (P24 speaker attribution -0.0127 with noise_std 0.0; P26 verified LLM rewrite -0.0142, noise 0.0072; P27 back-translation -0.0127, noise 0.0). Hypothesis: train-only surface asymmetry in frozen BERT embedding space, consistent with round-0's flagged failure mode. P26 is nonetheless ~+0.0085 above the unrepaired P15 (-0.0227), so label verification helps the family without rescuing it — at 289s, the worst cost/benefit in the round.
positive_signals: graft_donor_context with a same-label donor pool improves with copies_per_row 2->3 / multiplier 3.0->4.0 (P14 -> P21, +0.0090), the only above-noise gain observed so far.
Donor-label matters: same-label vs cross-label grafting differ by ~0.024 at identical 3.0x dose, giving the search a validated design constraint.
The winning family is also the cheapest (P21 0.032s, P22 0.009s), so dose can be increased further at essentially no processing-time penalty.
negative_signals: Cross-label context grafting (P22) is actively harmful (-0.0193 vs baseline), confirming that context is not a free perturbation slot.
Utterance-level paraphrase/rewrite families remain inert or harmful regardless of row selection (P23), retrieval-based composition (P25), verification (P26) or pivot control (P27).
Back-translation is now resolved unfavourably at 3.0x (P27, -0.0127) contradicting P04's single-seed +0.0016; the earlier positive is most plausibly seed/dose noise.
tradeoffs: P21's gain comes with the largest dataset multiplier of the round (4.00x); if dataset size is to be constrained, P14's 3.0x gives roughly two-thirds less data but ~0.009 lower F1.

P26 and P27 cost 289s and 230s respectively — 4 orders of magnitude above the grafting arms — while both underperform baseline, so external-generation and MT families are poor value at the current evaluation setup.
P23's margin probe adds 9.06s and a fold-internal SVM fit for a null F1 change and a dose shortfall (2.29x vs 2.5x designed).
uncertainties: P21 conflates copies_per_row (2->3) with total multiplier (3.0->4.0); which of the two drives the +0.0090 is unknown, and the +0.0135 vs baseline is only ~1.5x its noise_std, so the ceiling of the dose curve is unmapped.

P24 and P27 report noise_std 0.0 despite declaring three seeds, implying effectively deterministic pipelines; their dispersion is unestimated and their negative deltas cannot be bounded by measured variance.

P25's realized 3.91x does not match either declared sweep point (3.0x / 2.0x) and only one aggregate F1 was returned, so the concatenation family's dose-response and its near-null verdict are unresolved.
leads_from_this_round: Extend the graft_donor_context dose curve beyond 4.0x and separately vary copies_per_row at fixed multiplier (and vice versa) to disentangle pairing diversity from row count; cost is near-zero, so the main trade-off is dataset-size multiplier growth.

Constrain donor selection within the same label (e.g. speaker-matched, similarity-matched, or context-length-matched donors, or partial replacement of only some context turns) — the cross-label collapse in P22 shows donor identity carries label information, so a sharper donor criterion is the natural next lever.

Test whether the grafting benefit survives when mixed with an inert utterance-level op (e.g. P25's same-label neighbour concatenation, which was neutral at ~3.9x) versus grafting alone at matched dose, to check whether utterance-side edits dilute or compound the context-side gain.

round_analysis.summary: Round 3 decomposed the leading cross-example same-label recombination family at a matched ~4.0x dose. Three arms land in a statistically indistinguishable top cluster with history best P21 (0.72658): P34 donor-utterance swap (0.72645, +0.0134 vs baseline, noise_std 0.0106), P32 similarity-selected donor contexts (0.72563, +0.0126, noise_std 0.0096) and P31 concentrated-coverage grafting (0.72127, +0.0082, noise_std 0.0039). No arm beat the history best; the largest gap to P21 among top arms is within or near its own noise_std. Arms that changed the mechanism rather than its parameters all fell back toward baseline: turn-level partial splicing (P33, -0.0006 vs baseline), context turn-order permutation (P35, +0.0017), additive donor prepend (P37, +0.0030) and graft+WordNet compounding (P36, +0.0038). The strongest new mechanistic result is that the benefit is not context-specific: replacing the utterance while keeping the row's own context (P34) matches replacing the context while keeping the utterance (P21), suggesting a generic label-conditioned whole-component recombination effect rather than an incongruity-modelling effect.

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity is good for the dose-matched arms: realized multipliers are 3.995 (P31), 3.996 (P32), 3.967 (P33), 4.000 (P34), 3.993 (P36) against a designed 4.0x, so the coverage/donor-selection/granularity/component contrasts were implemented as intended. P37 realized 3.83x (below the 4.0x target, plausibly dedupe loss) and P35 realized 2.886x against a designed 3.0-4.0x, so those two arms are mildly under-dosed and their null results are weaker evidence. On outcome: the decomposition did discriminate mechanisms (full replacement > partial splice; replacement > additive; recombination alone > recombination + lexical edit), so the round's diagnostic goal was met, but the premise that a specific sub-axis of the context-grafting family carries the gain is not supported - the component-swap mirror (P34) reproduces the effect, and no arm exceeded the prior best beyond noise.

key_findings: Component specificity is refuted at matched 4.0x dose: P34 (graft_donor_utterance, scope utterance only, own context kept) reaches 0.72645 vs P21's 0.72658 - a 0.00014 gap against P34's noise_std of 0.0106. Mechanism hypothesis: the gain comes from label-conditioned recombination of whole components creating many new (context, utterance) embedding pairs around each label, i.e. an input-space label-preserving mixup/regularizer for the SVM, not from preserving or manufacturing utterance-context incongruity. Caveat: P34 assumes sarcasm travels with the utterance alone; the F1 result is consistent with that assumption but does not prove per-row label correctness.

Splice granularity matters more than donor selection. P33 (splice_partial_donor_turns, turn_replace_ratio 0.5, preserve_context_length/speaker_slots) is the only arm at or below baseline (-0.0006, noise_std 0.0032) and sits 0.0142 below P21 (>4x its noise_std), while P32's similarity-ranked donor pool (top-k=15, TF-IDF fold-internal) is statistically tied with uniform random donors. Hypothesis: half-replaced contexts produce hybrid dialogues that are neither the original nor a coherent donor, injecting label-uninformative noise, whereas whole-component swaps stay inside the corpus surface distribution.

Replacement beats addition and beats compounding at similar budget. P37 (prepend_donor_context, 2 additive + 1 replacement copy, realized 3.83x) gives +0.0030 vs baseline and sits 0.0105 below P21; P36 (graft + wordnet_synonym_replace_utterance on 50% of copies) gives +0.0038 and sits 0.0098 below P21 (noise_std 0.0067). Hypothesis: deleting the row's own context is part of the working mechanism (additive keeps the original pairing and lengthens context beyond typical corpus lengths), and the previously-inert WordNet edit dilutes rather than compounds the recombination signal - consistent with all earlier surface-rewriting families losing F1.

Coverage appears to matter more than pairings-per-row, but only weakly. P31 (select_random_row_subset fraction 0.5, copies_per_row 6, realized 3.995x) scores 0.0053 below P21 (100% coverage, 3 copies) at the same multiplier, about 1.35x P31's noise_std (0.0039). Hypothesis: every training row needs at least one grafted variant for the regularization to reach it; concentrating copies on half the rows leaves the other half unregularized. This is suggestive, not established, given the small gap and single-arm evidence.
positive_signals: graft_donor_utterance (P34, utterance-only same-label swap, 4.0x) matches the history best F1 at 0.0262s processing time - roughly 1/7 of P32's cost and 1/16 of P36's - making it the cheapest arm in the top cluster.

Whole-component same-label recombination (context or utterance) is reproducibly above baseline: P21 (+0.0135 history), P34 (+0.0134), P32 (+0.0126), P31 (+0.0082), all exceeding baseline by more than their own noise_std except P31 which is ~2x its noise_std.
Mixing the two grafting directions is untested and now motivated: P21 and P34 modify disjoint fields at the same dose and both work, so their combination is an evidence-backed opening.
negative_signals: Partial turn-level splicing (P33) erased the family's gain entirely (-0.0006 vs baseline) despite matched dose and preserved speaker slots - partial context corruption looks actively harmful.

Within-example structural perturbation (P35, permute/reverse context turn order) gave only +0.0017 (noise_std 0.0051) at 2.89x, i.e. indistinguishable from baseline; turn order appears to carry little usable signal for BERT+SVM, or the perturbation is too weak at this realized dose.
Similarity-based donor selection (P32, TF-IDF top-k=15) bought no F1 over uniform random donors while multiplying augmentation time by ~6x (0.190s vs 0.0217s for P31-style random grafting).
tradeoffs: P32: F1 statistically tied with random-donor grafting but augmentation_processing_time is 0.1897s vs 0.0262s (P34) / 0.0217s (P31) - a large cost for no measured primary gain.
P36: worst time in the round (0.4296s, ~87x baseline) and a lower F1 than plain grafting at equal 4.0x dose - cost and metric both move the wrong way.
P35: cheapest non-trivial arm (0.0129s) and lowest multiplier (2.886x, below its own 3.0-4.0x design target), but the F1 gain is inside noise, so the low cost does not buy a reliable benefit.
uncertainties: The top cluster (P21 0.72658, P34 0.72645, P32 0.72563) spans 0.001 F1 while individual noise_std values reach 0.0106 - the ranking within this cluster is not resolvable from this round, and even each arm's advantage over baseline is only 1.3-3.4x its own noise_std.

P37 reports noise_std = 0.0, which is implausible for a randomized donor-sampling pipeline; it may reflect a single seed or a deterministic seeding path, so P37's null result should be treated as having an unknown variance estimate rather than a tight one.

P35 (2.886x) and P37 (3.83x) are under-dosed relative to the other arms, so their weaker F1 could partly reflect lower multiplier rather than a weaker mechanism; the coverage conclusion from P31 also rests on a single arm and a sub-noise-to-1.35-noise gap.
Timing values come from single runs with no repeated-run variance, so cost comparisons are directional only.
leads_from_this_round: Combine the two whole-component swaps at a shared 4.0x budget: mix graft_donor_context copies (P21-style) with graft_donor_utterance copies (P34-style), and/or swap both fields from the same same-label donor pair, to test whether the effect is additive or saturating; both parents sit at the top of the cluster and both are cheap (<0.03s).

Resolve the top cluster with seed replication rather than new mechanisms: re-run P21, P34 and P32 under matched multi-seed protocols before spending further arms, since current gaps (<=0.001) are far below the observed noise_std (up to 0.0106).

Probe the coverage axis directly with graft_donor_context/graft_donor_utterance while holding copies_per_row=3 and varying select_random_row_subset fraction (e.g. 0.5 vs 0.75 vs 1.0) at fixed 4.0x-equivalent dose, since P31 hints coverage dominates copies-per-row; also consider dropping similarity-ranked donor pools and WordNet compounding from future arms given their cost-without-gain profile.

round_analysis.summary: Round 4 ran seven arms around the label-conditioned whole-component grafting family at a nominal 4.0x budget. Every grafting variant (P41 dual-source 0.7230, P42 mixed swap directions 0.7261, P43 coverage sweep 0.7265, P46 difficulty-allocated 0.7269, P47 topic-decorrelated 0.7234) landed in a tight 0.723-0.727 band, i.e. +0.010 to +0.014 weighted F1 vs baseline (~0.7130) but all within or near their own noise_std (0.0032-0.0101) of the history best (~0.7266). The one decisive result is the confound control P44: distinctness-preserving near-identity replication at the same 4.0x dose scored 0.7059, below baseline, showing that raw row count/copies is not the active ingredient and can even hurt. The speaker-coherence repair P45 (0.7145) again underperformed plain context grafting, a third negative for the speaker-identity family. P46 is nominal history best (+0.00029, ~10x smaller than its noise_std 0.0032) at ~2700x the augmentation time (53.94s vs ~0.02s). P43's realized multiplier was 6.94x, not the designed 4.0x, so its coverage comparison is not usable.

hypothesis_result.reason: Sub-question (a) was answered cleanly and in the hypothesized direction: P44 (surface_neutral_perturb, copies_per_row=3, coverage=1.0, realized 4.0x) scored 0.7059, worse than baseline and ~0.021 below the grafting cluster, so equal row count without new label-consistent (context,utterance) pairings does not reproduce the gain; the dose-vs-information confound resolves in favour of pairing novelty. Sub-question (b) was not supported: none of the novelty-increasing levers at fixed 4x (P42 mixed directions 0.7261, P47 topic-decorrelated donors 0.7234, P46 margin-based copy allocation 0.7269) separated from the existing history best by more than their noise_std, indicating a plateau rather than additivity. Sub-question (c) is not supported in the hypothesized direction: P45 speaker remapping scored 0.7145, clearly below the plain-graft cluster, so speaker coherence is not a hidden requirement. One arm is inconclusive on fidelity: P43 designed a two-point coverage sweep at a held-constant 4.0x but realized 6.94x overall multiplier, consistent with the two sweep points being unioned instead of reported separately, so its coverage conclusion cannot be read.

key_findings.finding: Dose is not the mechanism: at matched 4.0x and full coverage, near-identity replication (P44, surface_neutral_perturb, no field replacement) reached 0.7059 vs 0.7230-0.7269 for all grafting arms and vs ~0.7130 baseline. This is the strongest controlled comparison of the round, since P44 differs from P43/P46 mainly in whether the copy contains a new label-consistent cross-example pairing.
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Inert duplicated rows may act as sample-weight inflation for the original 690 rows, sharpening the SVM decision boundary on memorized surface features and effectively shrinking regularization; genuine cross-example recombination instead injects decorrelated (context, utterance) pairs that the model cannot memorize. Hypothesis, not established.

key_findings.finding: The grafting family has plateaued around 0.723-0.727 regardless of which novelty lever is pulled. P42 (mixing context-graft 2 copies + utterance-graft 1 copy), P47 (cross-cluster topic-distant donors), P41 (fully synthetic dual-donor rows with no tie to the original row) and P46 (difficulty-weighted copy allocation) are all within ~0.004 of each other, smaller than the per-arm noise_std (0.0032-0.0101).
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Consistent with a saturating input-space regularizer: once each row has ~3 label-consistent recombined variants, the extra decorrelation from smarter donor choice, mixed swap directions or hard-row targeting adds no further constraint on the BERT+SVM decision boundary. P41's parity also suggests the augmented row need not retain any component of the source row, only its label.

key_findings.finding: Speaker-identity manipulation failed a third time in its most in-distribution form: P45 (graft_donor_context + remap_donor_speakers_to_recipient_cast, bijective, in-text mentions remapped) scored 0.7145, ~0.012 below the plain-graft cluster and only +0.0015 vs baseline, at nearly double the processing time (0.0371s).
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Two competing explanations: (i) speaker coherence is genuinely irrelevant for this BERT+SVM setup, or (ii) map_in_text_mentions=true corrupted dialogue text (wrong-name substitutions inside utterances), injecting label-irrelevant noise that partially cancels the grafting gain. The second is a confounder that the current design cannot separate.

key_findings.finding: P46's nominal history-best status is not evidentially meaningful, and its cost is extreme: +0.00029 vs history best against noise_std 0.0032, with augmentation_processing_time 53.94s versus 0.018-0.022s for all other grafting arms (~2700x). The fold-internal probe (inner_cv=3 BERT+SVM fits) dominates that cost.
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Difficulty-based copy allocation changes only how the same 4.0x budget is distributed; if the regularizer saturates after the first grafted copy per row (coverage=1.0 was preserved), re-allocating extra copies to low-margin rows has little leverage. Consistent with the earlier inert result of difficulty selection on the paraphrase substrate.

positive_signals: P44 (dose_isolation_control, 4.0x, near-identity copies) at 0.7059 provides a clean negative control that isolates novel label-consistent pairings as the active ingredient of the grafting family.

P41 (compose_dual_donor_row, utterance from donor A, context from donor B, label preserved) reached 0.7230 (+0.0099 vs baseline) with the cheapest processing time of the round (0.0211s), showing fully synthetic same-label rows retain most of the effect without needing the source row's content.

P42 (graft_donor_context x2 + graft_donor_utterance x1, realized 3.978x) at 0.7261 confirms the two validated swap directions are interchangeable/compatible and can be freely mixed at negligible cost (0.0182s).
negative_signals: No arm beat the history best by more than its noise_std; the round produced no reliable primary-metric improvement over prior rounds.

P47 (cluster_training_rows k=8 + cross-cluster farthest-50% donors) at 0.7234 did not exceed uniform-random donors, while costing ~7x more time (0.1514s) — donor-similarity engineering has now failed in both directions (P32 similar donors, P47 dissimilar donors).
P45 (speaker remapping) at 0.7145 is a third consecutive negative for the speaker-identity family and actively degrades an otherwise working graft.
tradeoffs: P46 buys at most a noise-level primary gain (+0.00029, noise_std 0.0032) for a ~2700x augmentation_processing_time increase (53.94s vs ~0.02s); by the user's F1-first priority this is not disqualifying, but the gain is unproven so the cost is currently unjustified.

P43 attained the round's second-highest F1 (0.7265) while realizing 6.94x dataset size — roughly 1.7x more data than the 4x arms for no F1 separation, an unfavourable size/F1 trade if multiplier is to be kept small.
P47 pays ~7x processing time over plain grafting for a primary metric slightly below (within noise of) the uniform-donor reference.
uncertainties: P43's realized multiplier (6.94x) contradicts its designed fixed 4.0x budget and its per-sweep-point reporting requirement; the coverage=0.6 vs 1.0 question therefore remains open, and P43's score cannot be attributed to a specific coverage setting.

P44 reports noise_std = 0.0, unlike all other arms (0.0032-0.0101). It is unclear whether this reflects a single-seed run or a genuinely deterministic pipeline; if single-seed, its ~0.021 deficit is still large relative to other arms' noise but the exact magnitude is uncertain.

P45's deficit conflates 'speaker coherence is irrelevant' with 'in-text mention remapping damaged the text'; without an arm that remaps context_speakers only (map_in_text_mentions=false), the speaker family's verdict is not clean.

leads_from_this_round.lead: Probe the low end of the dose curve for the grafting operator (graft_donor_context / compose_dual_donor_row) at copies_per_row=1 and 2 (~2x-3x) with coverage=1.0, since the 4x and accidental 6.94x points are indistinguishable; a matched-F1 result at 2x would improve the size multiplier and cost with no primary-metric loss.
leads_from_this_round.evidence: P41/P42/P46/P47 cluster at 0.723-0.727 at ~4x and P43 at 6.94x reaches 0.7265, all within noise_std of each other.

leads_from_this_round.lead: Disentangle the speaker result with a minimal-variant graft that changes only context_speakers labels (map_in_text_mentions=false, reserve_recipient_speaker on/off) against plain graft_donor_context, to test whether P45's loss came from in-text name corruption rather than from speaker coherence being irrelevant.
leads_from_this_round.evidence: P45 = 0.7145 vs plain-graft cluster ~0.726, at ~2x processing time; its remap step edited utterance/context text as well as the speaker fields.

leads_from_this_round.lead: If difficulty targeting is revisited, replace the inner_cv=3 BERT+SVM probe with a cheap fold-internal proxy (single SVM margin fit, or a text-statistic proxy) and run with multiple seeds, since the current gain (+0.00029) is an order of magnitude below noise_std (0.0032) while costing 53.94s.
leads_from_this_round.evidence: P46 primary delta vs history best is far inside its own noise band; its allocation step preserved coverage=1.0, so only copy distribution differed from P43-style uniform allocation.

round_analysis.summary: Round 5 kept every arm inside the 2-4x band with realized multipliers matching targets and near-zero processing time. Two of the three provisional questions got informative answers. (1) Dose saturation: P51 at the minimum admissible dose (1 copy/row, realized 2.0x) reached 0.72704 weighted F1, +0.0140 vs baseline (0.71304) and +0.00016 vs history best (0.72687) — a difference far inside its noise_std (0.0047), i.e. statistically indistinguishable from the 4x grafting best while halving the size multiplier and costing 0.015s. (2) New mechanisms: only speaker-metadata donor conditioning (P56, 4x) moved the needle, 0.73152, +0.0185 vs baseline and +0.0046 vs history best (~1.0 noise_std, 0.0044) — a new nominal history best but only borderline reliable; multi-donor slot assembly (P52, 0.72305) and class-prior-conditioned copy allocation (P54, 0.72231) both landed within ~1.2 and ~0.5 noise_std of the grafting plateau, adding nothing. (3) Label locus: P55 (opposite-label donor context, label taken from the donor context) collapsed to 0.64885, -0.0642 vs baseline and well below the dose-matched P22 utterance-label control (0.6937), which is far larger than its noise_std (0.0102). P53, the minimal speaker-field-only repair, returned 0.72372, within its own noise band (0.0069) of the plain-graft arms, so speaker-field coherence alone is neutral.
secondary_metrics: dataset size multiplier after augmentation (direction unspecified; band-constrained 2-4x)

hypothesis_result.reason: Design fidelity is good on the quantities that were measured: realized multipliers (2.0, 3.9996, 4.0, 3.0, 2.9996, 4.0) match every target, and all arms report the intended per-fold, training-only donor construction. Sub-question 1 is supported — the minimum dose P51 matches the 4x grafting plateau within noise, so the benefit saturates after one label-consistent recombined variant. Sub-question 3 is answered decisively in the negative direction predicted as a risk: transferring the label with the imported context (P55) is worse than transferring it with the utterance (P22), so the sarcasm label lives predominantly in the utterance. Sub-question 2 is only weakly supported: of three untested information sources, two (multi-donor slot assembly, class-prior allocation) stayed inside the plateau, and the one nominal gain (P56 speaker-conditioned donor pool) is roughly one noise_std above the previous best and its declared fallback-usage diagnostic was not reported, leaving open whether the arm partly collapsed onto plain grafting.

key_findings.finding: Grafting dose is effectively saturated at the minimum: P51 (copies_per_row=1, realized 2.0x) equals the 4x grafting best within noise (delta +0.00016 vs history best, noise_std 0.0047) at half the data volume and 0.015s.
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Hypothesis: same-label context grafting acts as a context-invariance regularizer for the BERT+SVM pipeline — once the model has seen each utterance paired with one alternative same-label context, the 'context is not diagnostic on its own' signal is already delivered; extra copies re-sample the same low-entropy transformation and add no new information, only redundant rows.
key_findings.evidence: P51 vs history-best 4x graft (P21/P43 lineage); also consistent with the Round-4 P44 dose control (0.7059).

key_findings.finding: Speaker-metadata donor conditioning (P56) is the only arm above the plateau: 0.73152, +0.0046 vs history best, +0.0078 vs the dose-matched P53 plain-graft repair, at identical 4x dose and identical graft operator.
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Hypothesis: requiring the recipient's speaker to appear in the donor's context_speakers yields grafted dialogues that are pragmatically plausible (the recipient is a participant, not an intruder), so the recombined rows stay on-manifold for BERT's sentence encoding while still breaking the spurious context-label association. Purely random grafting produces some incoherent rows that act as label-preserving noise.
key_findings.evidence: Controlled comparison P56 vs P53/P21-P43 at 4x, copies_per_row=3, coverage 1.0 — the only varied factor is build_speaker_conditioned_donor_pool (min_pool_size=5, fallback to uniform). Caveat: gain ~1.0 noise_std (0.0044) and fallback rate unreported.

key_findings.finding: The sarcasm label travels with the utterance, not the preceding context: P55 (donor-context label assignment) fell to 0.64885, below both baseline (-0.0642) and the utterance-label cross-label control P22 (0.6937), a gap several times noise_std (0.0102).
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Hypothesis: pairing an utterance with an opposite-label context and relabelling to the donor's label injects direct label noise on the utterance channel — the feature the classifier actually relies on. P22 at least preserved utterance-label consistency, which is why it degraded less. This implies future recombination must always preserve the utterance-label binding; only context is a safe recombination slot.
key_findings.evidence: P55 vs P22 dose-matched (2 copies, 3.0x), differing only in label_assignment source.

key_findings.finding: Two novel information sources produced no movement: multi-donor turn-slot assembly (P52, 0.72305) and class-prior-conditioned copy allocation (P54, 0.72231) both sit inside the grafting plateau band and are not reliably distinguishable from P51 given noise_std 0.0031 and 0.0086.
key_findings.mechanism_hypothesis: Hypothesis for P52: finer recombination granularity destroys intra-context discourse coherence without adding a new invariance beyond what whole-context grafting already teaches, so the added diversity is wasted or mildly harmful. Hypothesis for P54: the plateau is a saturation effect of the invariance signal rather than a class-imbalance effect, so re-weighting copies by class prior cannot help; the induced class-balance shift is a declared confounder against uniform-allocation 3x grafting.
key_findings.evidence: P52 and P54 vs P51/P53 within-round; P54 realized augmented class balance was not reported.

positive_signals: P56 speaker-conditioned donor pool: new nominal history best 0.73152 (+0.0185 vs baseline) at 4x, 0.127s — the largest baseline gain observed this round.
P51 minimum-dose graft: plateau-level F1 (0.72704) at the smallest multiplier (2.0x) and lowest cost among the 4x arms, giving a strictly better size/time profile for equal F1.
P53 confirms speaker-field remapping is F1-neutral (0.72372, within noise of plain graft), so metadata edits are safe to combine with other levers.
negative_signals: P55 label-locus diagnostic collapsed (0.64885, -0.0642 vs baseline): assigning the donor context's label is strongly harmful — retire label-transforming context grafts.
P52 multi-donor slot assembly gave the largest time cost of the round (0.275s, 55x baseline) for a nominally lower F1 than P51 at twice the multiplier.
P54 class-prior balancing produced no F1 gain while carrying the highest noise_std of the non-diagnostic arms (0.0086), i.e. it may also add instability.
tradeoffs: P56 vs P51: +0.0046 F1 (about one noise_std, not clearly reliable) is bought with 2x the dataset multiplier (4.0 vs 2.0) and ~8.5x the processing time (0.127s vs 0.015s); in absolute terms both times are negligible, so the real cost is data volume.
P51 vs the 4x grafting lineage: equal F1 within noise but halved multiplier — a clean secondary-metric win with no primary-metric loss, the best efficiency point of the round.
P52 pays both the highest time and a full 4x multiplier while sitting at or slightly below the 2x arm's F1 — dominated on all three metrics.
uncertainties: P56's declared fallback-usage rate was not reported; if a large fraction of rows fell back to the uniform same-label pool, the arm partially collapses onto plain grafting and its +0.0046 gain would be even harder to attribute to speaker conditioning.

The P56 vs previous-best gap (0.0046) is comparable to its noise_std (0.0044) and smaller than P53's noise_std (0.0069); with only three seeds per arm this round's ranking among all preserve-label graft variants is not securely established.

Processing times are single-measurement per arm with no repeated-run variance, so the P52 > P56 > P54 > P53 > P51 > P55 time ordering should be treated as indicative only; all values are sub-second and unlikely to drive decisions.

leads_from_this_round.lead: Combine the two independently supported levers: apply build_speaker_conditioned_donor_pool at the saturated minimum dose (copies_per_row=1, ~2.0x) instead of 3 copies/4x, to test whether the speaker-conditioning gain survives at the efficient dose point.
leads_from_this_round.evidence: P51 shows dose saturation at 2.0x; P56 shows the only above-plateau F1 at 4x; the two have never been crossed.
leads_from_this_round.expected_tradeoff: If F1 holds, this dominates P56 on multiplier and time; if F1 drops toward 0.727, it would indicate the speaker-conditioning effect needs dose to express itself.

leads_from_this_round.lead: Strengthen or vary the donor-pool coherence constraint (e.g. require full cast overlap, require the recipient speaker to occupy the last context turn, or report/limit fallback usage) to see whether the P56 direction is monotone rather than a single noisy point.
leads_from_this_round.evidence: P56 (speaker-overlap conditioning) beat dose-matched plain graft P53 by +0.0078 while topic/TF-IDF donor engineering previously failed, suggesting pragmatic plausibility rather than lexical similarity is the useful selection axis.
leads_from_this_round.expected_tradeoff: Tighter constraints shrink the donor pool, raising fallback rate and duplicate rejection, which may cap the achievable multiplier below 4x and increase processing time.

leads_from_this_round.lead: Given P55, shift novelty budget from label-transforming or context-only-label designs toward utterance-side augmentation that preserves the utterance-label binding (e.g. paraphrase or lexical perturbation of the target utterance with unchanged context), which the label-locus result identifies as the information-bearing channel and which the grafting family has never touched.
leads_from_this_round.evidence: P55 (-0.0642) vs P22 (-0.019 region) shows the label follows the utterance; all above-baseline arms so far only recombine context, i.e. the diagnostic channel has never been augmented.
leads_from_this_round.expected_tradeoff: Utterance edits risk flipping the true label (sarcasm is cue-fragile) and may add real processing time if a generative or embedding-based rewriter is used, unlike the near-free recombination arms.

round_analysis.summary: Round 6 spent two arms refining the round-5 speaker-conditioning signal and four on untouched mechanisms. No arm reached the history best (0.7315, P56). The best arm was P63 (structure-matched same-label context grafting, 3.0x, weighted F1 0.7266, +0.0135 vs baseline, -0.0050 vs history best — i.e. inside its own noise_std of 0.0092 of the history best), followed by P62 (addressee-coherent grafting, 4.0x, 0.7229, +0.0099 vs baseline). The speaker-conditioning follow-up at minimum dose (P61, 2.0x) fell back to baseline level (+0.0004, far below noise_std 0.0070), and the stricter coherence constraint at matched 4x dose (P62) did not reproduce P56, so the conditioning axis is not monotone. All three genuinely new mechanisms — class-prototype contexts (P64, -0.0025 vs baseline), full/partial context dropout (P65, -0.0054), and cue-preserving cross-example utterance word swap (P66, -0.0073, and 712x baseline processing time) — landed at or below baseline, most of them within ~1 noise_std, so they are best read as 'no gain' rather than clear damage.

hypothesis_result.reason: The exploration objective (>=half the budget on new mechanisms, all realized multipliers in 2-4x band) was met and produced interpretable negatives: prototypes, context dropout and utterance recombination all failed to beat baseline. But the primary resolution goal — whether P56's speaker-conditioning gain is real and dose-independent — is inconclusive: the promised per-fold fallback-rate diagnostic is absent from the measured gradient, so realized constraint strength for P61/P62/P63 cannot be verified, and P61/P62 differ from P56 in dose and constraint definition respectively rather than isolating one factor. Additionally P65 realized 2.80x and P66 realized 2.28x against 3.0x targets, so those two arms tested a lower effective dose than designed.

key_findings: Same-label context grafting remains the only family reliably above baseline, but donor-selection sophistication is not the lever: at matched 4.0x dose, tighter addressee+cast-overlap conditioning (P62, 0.7229) sits 0.0086 below the looser round-5 speaker-conditioned arm (P56, 0.7315) — about 1.3x P62's noise_std. Mechanism hypothesis: hard pragmatic constraints shrink the donor pool and reduce the diversity of grafted contexts, weakening the context-invariance regularizer; the unreported fallback ladder means the realized constraint could also have collapsed partly onto plain grafting, which would flatten the comparison.

The donor-diversity hypothesis is corroborated from the opposite extreme: P64 replaced individual donors with 4 per-label medoid prototypes at the same 4.0x dose and was the weakest grafting arm (0.7105, -0.0025 vs baseline, worse than P62 by 0.0124 and P63 by 0.0160). Grafting many copies of a handful of canonical contexts appears to add duplicated, low-entropy features rather than an invariance signal; this is a controlled comparison against P62/P64 differing mainly in donor entropy (dose matched at ~4x, both context-scope, label preserved).

Structural (turn-count + length-quartile) donor matching (P63) is the round's most efficient arm: highest F1 (0.7266) at a lower dose (3.0x) and at 0.144s versus 0.820s for P62 and 0.650s for P64. Hypothesis: shape-matched grafts keep the BERT context encoding on-manifold without over-restricting lexical/speaker content, i.e. plausibility constraints on form are cheaper and no worse than constraints on pragmatics — though its -0.0050 gap to history best is inside its noise_std, so P63 may simply be another point on the same plateau.

Both non-graft mechanisms failed in ways consistent with the utterance channel carrying the label. Full/partial context removal (P65, 0.7076) is worse than every cross-example graft, so grafting is not acting purely as 'ignore the context' regularization — an empty-context row likely also produces an out-of-distribution feature vector. Conversely, perturbing the utterance itself with cue-protected cross-example content-word swaps (P66, 0.7058) was the worst arm and by far the most expensive (3.49s), suggesting the top-PMI cue list did not capture the actual sarcasm-bearing surface signal (incongruity between utterance content and context), so swapping 'non-cue' content still broke the label binding.
positive_signals: P63 structure_matched_donor_pool + graft_donor_context (3.0x, context scope): 0.7266, +0.0135 vs baseline (~1.5 noise_std) at only 0.144s — best F1/cost point of the round and statistically indistinguishable from the history best.
P62 addressee_coherent grafting (4.0x): 0.7229, +0.0099 vs baseline, confirming the graft family stays above baseline across several different donor-selection rules.

Dose remains directionally relevant within the metadata-conditioned family: P61 at 2.0x (+0.0004) vs P62 at 4.0x (+0.0099), though the two arms also differ in donor constraint, so dose and constraint are confounded here.
negative_signals: P61 speaker-conditioned graft at minimum dose 2.0x returned to baseline (+0.0004, << noise_std 0.0070), so P56's above-plateau reading is not reproduced without the 4x volume.
P64 class-prototype grafting fell below baseline (-0.0025) despite matched 4x dose — low-entropy donor sets appear counterproductive for this regularizer.
P65 context dropout (-0.0054) and P66 cue-preserving utterance recombination (-0.0073) both below baseline; P66 additionally cost 3.49s (712x baseline) for the worst F1 in the round.
tradeoffs: P66: worst primary metric combined with the largest processing-time regression (3.49s vs 0.0049s baseline) and an under-target multiplier (2.28x vs 3.0x designed) — dominated on every axis.

P62 vs P63: P62 uses 5.7x more processing time (0.820s vs 0.144s) and a higher multiplier (3.99x vs 3.00x) yet scores 0.0037 lower — extra dose and pragmatic filtering bought nothing here, though the gap is inside noise_std.
P65 is the cheapest arm (0.0113s) and realized only 2.80x of the 3.0x target, but pays with a below-baseline F1; cheapness does not compensate given the user's F1 priority.
uncertainties: The per-fold fallback rates promised for P61/P62/P63 are not in the measured gradient, so realized donor-constraint strength is unknown; any of these arms may have partially collapsed onto uniform same-label grafting, which would make the 'conditioning is not monotone' reading unattributable.

All round-6 deltas against the history best (P56) are between 0.5 and 1.3 noise_std and single-seed, so P56 itself may be a seed-lucky point on a ~0.722-0.731 plateau rather than a distinct optimum; without multi-seed replication of P56 the whole conditioning question stays open.

P65 and P66 under-realized their target multipliers (2.80x, 2.28x), so their negative results confound mechanism with reduced effective dose; timing differences are single-run and have no repeated-run variance.
leads_from_this_round: Replicate the exact P56 configuration (speaker-in-donor-context, 4.0x graft_donor_context) with multiple seeds and with the fallback rate actually emitted, to decide whether the history best is a real above-plateau point before more conditioning variants are spent on it.

Treat donor-pool entropy, not donor plausibility, as the tunable axis: at fixed 4.0x dose, sweep the number of distinct donors per recipient / minimum pool size between the P64 extreme (4 prototypes) and unrestricted uniform same-label sampling, since P64 (low entropy) < P62 (constrained) < uniform-graft ordering points that way.

Push the cheap structural-matching arm (build_structure_matched_donor_pool, turn_count_tolerance=1, length quartile) to 4.0x dose and/or relax the length-quartile constraint, since P63 achieved the round's best F1 at 3.0x for 0.144s and its dose response is untested; watch that the multiplier increase does not repeat P64-style duplication.
